clue.text: Complex investigation involving father, fish and choppy sea

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: a choppy sea is rough and broken up, so its letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A tangled inquiry that somehow takes in dad, a fish and rough water.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper chase is a long trawl through documents, the sort of laborious bureaucratic probe a complex inquiry becomes.

clue.text: Purplish volcanic stone, with central portion removed

parts.note: pumice is a light porous rock formed from lava

explanation.definitionFit: Puce is a brownish-purple colour, so it describes something purplish.

clue.text: Favouring note of originality around one of dull texts

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: the note's letters go round the letter for one

a means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: Someone backing an original note in an otherwise tedious body of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: SIC, Latin for 'thus', is printed in square brackets after a quoted slip to show it was in the original.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosaic literally means relating to prose, and by extension plain and unexciting, so it fits writing that is flat and uninspired.

clue.text: Violent film? Override gross flicks

indicators.note: to flick is to jerk or flip something about, so the letters are tossed into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A critic complaining about crude films that push violence too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flicks' reads as films, matching the surface, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Reservoir Dogs is Quentin Tarantino's notoriously bloody 1992 crime movie, an example of a brutal picture.

clue.text: Ready confusion about playing card

indicators.note: the muddle word wraps round the rearranged card letters

parts.note: a hash is a muddle or mess

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are in play, moved about into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone flustered while holding a playing card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is not the adjective but 'the ready', British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The ready is informal for money available to spend, which is coins and notes in the hand.

clue.text: Descendant, even if not initially close one

definitions.text: Descendant, even if not initially close one

parts.words: Descendant, even if not initially close one
parts.note: the clue says the answer is a descendant, and would still mean one after losing the first letter of close and one (C and I): what remains is a three-letter word for a male child

explanation.surface: An heir who, though not the nearest relative at first, still counts.
explanation.walkthrough: Take C (first of 'close') and I (one) out of the answer and you get SON, which is also a descendant, so the answer means the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: A scion is an heir or offspring of a family line, a young member of the next generation.

clue.text: A filter's incomplete? That won't happen!

indicators.note: the sieve word is left unfinished, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a sift is a sieve or strainer, something that filters

explanation.surface: A broken strainer, and someone scoffing that it will ever be mended.
explanation.definitionFit: The scornful exclamation is an idiom of disbelief, meaning no chance of that ever coming true.

clue.text: Exceptional stone wine vault about to be eradicated

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight

indicators.note: the letter for about is wiped out of the vault word

parts.note: a cellar is an underground store for wine
c, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A wine cellar of outstanding stonework that is about to be demolished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stone' is the 14-pound unit of weight, abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellar means star-like and hence outstanding or brilliant, so it describes something exceptional.

clue.text: Writer experienced university course without money? On the contrary

explanation.walkthrough: The writer is a pen, not a person.

clue.text: Obstruct work as a breeder

definitions.meaning: breeders mix two varieties to produce a hybrid

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to thwart and to interbreed plants or animals of different kinds.

clue.text: Single one brought in to agitate monarch

sole means single or only
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.definitionFit: The Sun King was the nickname of Louis XIV of France, a famous monarch.

clue.text: Determine location of state train

parts.note: to orient is to find one's position or bearings
to express is to state or put into words

explanation.surface: Instructions to work out where a state railway service is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient Express is the famous luxury rail service between Paris and Istanbul.

clue.text: Representation of vital force in a tropical plant

indicators.note: a representation recasts something in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Depicting a plant as the embodiment of life force.

clue.text: Number of fish circling part of canal wall initially? Wait for the end of the day!

definitions.text: Wait for the end of the day!

indicators.note: the fish haul wraps round the canal piece and the initial

a lock is the gated section that raises and lowers boats on a canal

indicators.note: only the first letter of wall is used

explanation.surface: An angler's haul of fish around a canal lock, with a nudge to be patient.
explanation.definitionFit: To clock-watch is to keep eyeing the time, longing for knocking-off time at work.

clue.text: Spike goes round part of Scotland for sport

indicators.note: the spiking word surrounds the Scottish place

parts.note: to lace a drink is to spike it with alcohol

explanation.walkthrough: Ross is part of the old Highland county of Ross and Cromarty.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team game played with netted sticks, a sport of North American origin.

clue.text: Catch associate returning? Not quite

the associate word falls just short, its last letter lopped

explanation.walkthrough: After the turnaround the dropped R would sit at the front, which is why 'Not quite' removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap is to snare or trick someone into a trap, a synonym for to catch.

clue.text: Exclamation about B Pitt's partner ignoring one's flattery

explanation.surface: A shriek over Brad Pitt's partner, who brushes off sweet talk.

clue.text: Group of warriors in company animated about head of regiment

indicators.note: the heated word wraps round the regiment's first letter

indicators.note: only the first letter of regiment is taken

explanation.definitionFit: A cohort was a division of a Roman legion, a body of soldiers.

clue.text: Deer by Lake, say, showing rear limb

eg, for example, means say

explanation.definitionFit: A hind leg is one of an animal's back legs, a posterior limb.

clue.text: Film's opening — one capturing each ugly person

the card word holds the word each inside it

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards

clue.text: Composer's centrepiece unfavourably thrown over

clue.text: Bounder chasing bereaved women seen around new woman in mall?

clue.text: Earth receiving trace of planetary damage
